content: Fluconazole is a medication used to treat vaginal yeast infections by inhibiting the growth of common fungal organisms responsible for such infections. It is important to read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting this medication and each time you receive a refill. In Canada, some brands of fluconazole are available without a prescription. The effects of this medication may persist for several days after administration. How to Use: Take fluconazole exactly as directed by your healthcare provider. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Side Effects: Common side effects of fluconazole include nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, headache, and dizziness. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks. Rarely, fluconazole may cause serious liver disease or a severe allergic reaction. This is not a comprehensive list of side effects. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. In the United States, you can report side effects to the FDA, and in Canada, you can report them to Health Canada. Precautions: Before taking fluconazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other azole antifungal drugs (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Fluconazole may cause a condition known as QT prolongation, which affects the heart rhythm. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also increase this risk. Conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting, or the use of certain medications like diuretics (water pills), may exacerbate this risk. Fluconazole may cause dizziness in some individuals. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can intensify this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: During pregnancy, fluconazole should only be used when clearly necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby if taken during the first three months of pregnancy. Fluconazole passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Consult your doctor before using this medication if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of fluconazole or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Fluconazole can slow the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting how they work. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, you can call 1-844-764-7669. Storage: Store fluconazole at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for guidance on safe disposal. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about fluconazole. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
